verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean states the same six scaling laws, but parameterized by an abstract chart length l and velocity factor c instead of by powers of Q; the paper's exponents are recovered by the repository's own substitutions l = MeanChartCompatibility.chartScale n = Q^(-1/2) (the chart is R = r/sqrt Q, cf. the docstring of SignedStressPrimitive.lengthScale) and c = Q^(-A), each row then being one rpow_sub/ring step. Row by row: sourceMoment_coverPull gives moment-weight m a factor u/l^(m+1), so with u = Q^(-A) and m = 2, 1 it gives Q^(-(A-3/2)) and Q^(-(A-1)), i.e. the M_θ and M_z rows; measured_debt_on and sourceDebt_coverPull give the triple (P, J_θ, J_z) the factors c², c²/l³, c²/l², i.e. Q^(-2A), Q^(-(2A-3/2)), Q^(-(2A-1)), the P, J_θ and J_z rows; rho_second_moment_scale plus the definition pressureCoefficient = base * (length)² gives c_ρ ∝ ℓ², i.e. the Q^(-1) row. Only the P row's Q-exponent arithmetic appears explicitly as a declaration (pressure_unit_factor, stress_unit_factor: Q^(-(2A+1/2))/Q^(-1/2) = Q^(-2A)); no declaration was found that writes the exponents A-3/2, A-1, 2A-3/2, 2A-1 or -1 in powers of Q, and no declaration was found that collects the six rows into one table.
